textbookText: 81. The lower fixed point of a thermometer is determined using: A) Pure melting ice at standard atmospheric pressure B) Boiling water at standard atmospheric pressure C) Human body temperature D) Room temperature

82. In a constant-pressure gas thermometer, temperature is related to gas volume by: A) Volume increasing linearly with absolute temperature (Charles's law behavior) B) Volume remaining constant regardless of temperature C) Pressure increasing linearly with volume at constant temperature D) Volume decreasing as temperature increases
83. Fever in the human body is generally indicated by an oral temperature above approximately: A) 37.5–38°C B) 35°C C) 42°C D) 30°C

84. Which of the following scales was historically defined using the freezing point of a salt-ice mixture as its zero? A) Fahrenheit scale B) Celsius scale C) Kelvin scale D) Réaumur scale (defined by pure water freezing/boiling, not salt-ice — distractor check)
85. The SI unit of temperature is: A) Kelvin (K) B) Celsius (°C) C) Fahrenheit (°F) D) Joule (J)

86. A thermometer's sensitivity is improved by: A) Using a bulb with thin walls and a capillary tube of very fine bore B) Using a thick-walled bulb C) Using a wide-bore capillary tube D) Increasing the length of the stem only, without changing the bulb

87. Which statement correctly distinguishes heat and temperature? A) Heat is energy (measured in joules); temperature is a state variable indicating hotness level (measured in kelvin) B) Heat and temperature are the same physical quantity with different names C) Temperature is measured in joules, heat in kelvin D) Heat always flows from cold to hot bodies spontaneously
88. On the Kelvin scale, the boiling point of water at standard pressure is: A) 373.15 K B) 273.15 K C) 100 K D) 0 K

89. Why can't temperature go below absolute zero (a genuinely extraordinary physical limit)? A) At absolute zero, the classical translational kinetic energy of particles would be at its theoretical minimum, so no lower thermal state exists B) Because thermometers are not calibrated below 0°C C) Because the Fahrenheit scale has no negative numbers D) Because water always freezes before that point
90. Convert 25°C to Fahrenheit: A) 77°F B) 45°F C) 57°F D) 98.6°F
